title: Fewer runs. Better questions.
scope: Research proposals, not launched jobs or predicted gains. Choose settings using held-out Fleet task success, never WebExploitBench results. Exact model, data, runtime, costs and evaluation settings must be frozen before launch.

defaults.sampling: All eligible assistant targets once per epoch; no extra weight for the final submission
defaults.loss: Assistant-token cross-entropy; mask user text, tool observations and repeated context
defaults.split: Freeze family-grouped train/dev/final before extracting examples
defaults.eval: Same frozen OpenCode program, tools, model precision and time/token budgets for base and trained models
defaults.selection: Fleet dev task success; uncertainty across task families and separate training seeds
defaults.telemetry: W&B numeric training loss, supervised/context tokens, gradient norm, LR, steps, time, memory, checkpoints and Fleet dev outcomes; no private content
defaults.checkpoint: Recoverable checkpoint at least every 50 updates and each epoch; verify resume, changed weights and complete export
defaults.proposed_not_qualified: The main-branch SFT wrapper currently hardcodes constant LR with no warmup and rejects Qwen LoRA. The proposed cosine schedule, LoRA and exact long-context placement need implementation/qualification. This generator is not a job launcher.

datasets.Broad teacher: All currently eligible successful teacher sessions on TRAIN families, deduplicated. Freeze a new manifest and publish actual family/session/token counts; do not assume the old 75-task or 3,000-session snapshot is current.
datasets.Matched teacher: Teacher sessions restricted to families also solved by the exact base Qwen under the matched tool program. Freeze the same per-family supervised-token budget as Matched self and Matched 50:50.
datasets.Matched self: Only successful exact-base Qwen sessions, on the identical family intersection and per-family token budgets as Matched teacher. If source tools, context or success evidence differ, report that difference or defer the comparison.
datasets.Matched 50:50: Half teacher and half exact-base Qwen by supervised-token weight within each shared family, not by number of sessions. Match total tokens and family weights to both pure-source arms.

controls.title: Teach the whole attempt
controls.text: Cover reconnaissance, testing, revisions and reporting—not just the final answer. Mask copied history and tool results. Count unique supervised tokens, their duplicates, and coverage of early/middle/late actions. A packed example is a sequence assembled to use the training context efficiently; it is not a task or a complete rollout.

controls.title: Keep 262k as the starting context
controls.text: The default cap is 262,144 tokens, not a promise that every example is that long. Keep original model-visible history and recorded compactions. The optional 65,536-token experiment must preserve target coverage and explicitly document lost earlier context; never silently truncate long attempts. Node count comes from an exact memory/throughput test, not the context number alone.

controls.title: Freeze data before tuning
controls.text: Keep every version and session of a task family in one partition. Balance applications, vulnerability categories and difficulty when feasible; publish remaining imbalance. Do not recycle old dev/final families into expanded training. If a clean expanded split is impossible, declare a new study and disclose prior exposure. Splitting families does not hold out entire applications.

controls.title: Spend on task success
controls.text: Run the same Fleet development tasks and rollout seeds for each candidate. Training loss checks optimization; it does not choose the winner. Report paired task differences and uncertainty. Do not promote a model because one extra tiny-sample success looks impressive. Freeze final checkpoints before report-only WebExploitBench comparisons.

sources.title: CTF-Dojo · closest task match
sources.observed: Qwen3 family including 32B; 486 execution-verified training trajectories after a 32,768-token filter; full SFT, batch 16, LR 5e-6, two epochs.
sources.use: Anchor our first full-SFT row here.
sources.limit: Different Qwen generation, mixed CTF categories and much shorter inputs. This is not an exact Fleet/Qwen3.8 recipe.

sources.title: OpenThoughts-Agent · similar-size tool user
sources.observed: Qwen3-32B, 100k agent demonstrations, full SFT: LR 4e-5, batch 96, five epochs, 32,768 context, cosine schedule, 10% warmup.
sources.use: Supports exploring substantially higher LR and repeated passes, not just 1e-6 tweaks.
sources.limit: Far larger, broader data. We start below its LR and do not copy five epochs or batch 96 blindly.

sources.title: OpenThoughts-Agent · data comes first
sources.observed: More than 100 controlled data-pipeline experiments examined sources, task diversity, teacher choice and trajectory filtering.
sources.use: Prioritize broad valid Fleet data and controlled teacher/self comparisons alongside LR.
sources.limit: Borrow the experimental method, never the external task data. Short-trace filtering is a hypothesis, not an automatic Fleet exclusion.

sources.title: OpenThinker-32B · open training recipe
sources.observed: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, full SFT: LR 1e-5, global batch 96, three epochs, 16,384 context, cosine and 10% warmup.
sources.use: A second same-size recipe supports a middle LR range and explicit schedule control.
sources.limit: Reasoning rather than interactive exploitation; neither its batch nor token length is our optimum.

sources.title: LoRA Without Regret · compare fairly
sources.observed: LoRA needs its own LR tuning; updating feed-forward layers matters, and larger batches can widen the gap to full training.
sources.use: Test all-linear-layer LoRA at 5e-5 and 2e-4, with the same modest batch as full SFT.
sources.limit: Those two rates and rank 64 are our starting choices. LoRA is not automatically faster at 262k context.

sources.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
sources.observed: Separately tuned full and LoRA experiments on Llama2-7B code/math used ranks 16/64/256, all transformer modules and alpha = 2 × rank; capacity and forgetting differed.
sources.use: Start at rank 64, alpha 128; only investigate rank 256 if tuned rank 64 underfits.
sources.limit: Different model and training conditions. Keep retention checks and task outcomes; do not declare either method universally better.

sources.title: Hyperband · staged compute allocation
sources.observed: Allocates resources adaptively across candidates instead of fully training every combination.
sources.use: Screen a small broad set, then spend on promising candidates and repeats.
sources.limit: Our plan is inspired by this principle, not a Hyperband implementation. Do not stop cyber runs early solely because imitation loss falls slowly.

sources.title: Exact Qwen3.8 model context
sources.observed: The model card specifies a native context of 262,144 tokens.
sources.use: Retain the requested long-context setting as the starting point.
sources.limit: Inference context support does not prove a particular training implementation fits in two or eight nodes.

sources.title: DeepSeekMath · RL comparison method
sources.observed: Group Relative Policy Optimization compares scored responses to the same prompt without a separate value model.
sources.use: A starting algorithm for a small, controlled RL ladder.
sources.limit: Math responses are not hours-long tool episodes. Our LR, group sizes and 32-update budget are engineering hypotheses, not copied cyber results.

sft.title: SFT · learn from saved successes
columns: Priority and expandable research question. These are proposals, not running jobs.
The frozen source pool. Matched arms use the same families and supervised-token weights.
Full updates all eligible model weights. LoRA trains added low-rank matrices; rank sets their capacity.
Peak size of an optimization step. 5e-6 means 0.000005.
Effective training examples per optimizer update across all devices, including accumulated microbatches. Also record actual supervised tokens/update.
Complete passes through this row’s frozen training examples. Different data pools need not have equal token counts.
Maximum tokens visible in one training example, including history. Not an episode time limit.
Work in stages. Later rows inherit the first-stage Fleet-dev winner only after it is explicitly selected.

runs.name: Broad teacher anchor
runs.question: Does broad, correctly extracted teacher data improve task success?
runs.why: Closest task-matched published starting point; use all eligible train data, not another tiny pilot.
runs.compare: Exact base Qwen with identical evaluation settings.
runs.gate: Freeze data/targets/split; qualify proposed cosine schedule and exact long-context runtime.

runs.name: Stronger learning rate
runs.question: Is our starting rate leaving useful learning on the table?
runs.why: A fourfold change is informative. Related 32B recipes use 1e-5 to 4e-5.
runs.gate: Same examples, split, seed, tokens and schedule as S01.

runs.name: Gentler learning rate
runs.question: Does the stronger intervention damage useful behavior?
runs.why: The low edge distinguishes under-learning from overshooting across a 20× LR range.
runs.gate: Same examples, split, seed, tokens and schedule as S01.

runs.name: Matched teacher control
runs.question: What can we learn on the exact families Qwen also solves?
runs.why: An essential control before claiming self demonstrations are better or worse.
runs.compare: S05/S06; do not compare source quality directly against broader S01.
runs.gate: Freeze family intersection and identical per-family supervised-token weights; do not demand unavailable self data.

runs.name: Matched self successes
runs.question: Are Qwen’s own successful actions easier for it to learn from?
runs.why: Tests imitation source rather than changing family difficulty and data volume at the same time.
runs.compare: S04; source changes, family weights and training-token budget do not.
runs.gate: Accept exact-base Qwen success records and reconstruct original model-visible tool context.

runs.name: Matched half-and-half
runs.question: Does combining teacher and self examples help?
runs.why: Tests complementary solution styles without replacing the broad-data anchor.
runs.compare: S04/S05; match family weights and total supervised tokens.
runs.gate: 50:50 by supervised-token weight within each family; publish exclusions.

runs.name: One pass
runs.question: Would half as much training preserve the gain?
runs.why: Spend less if the useful learning arrives early.
runs.gate: Choose S01/S02/S03 using Fleet dev first; train afresh with its own full cosine schedule.

runs.name: Four passes
runs.question: Does repetition improve task success beyond two passes?
runs.why: A meaningful duration contrast; four is conditional, not an instruction to train indefinitely.
runs.compare: First-stage winner; only planned epochs change.
runs.gate: Fleet dev justifies more training; start from base with a four-pass cosine schedule, not an epoch-2 checkpoint relabeled as a four-pass run.

runs.name: Larger batch
runs.question: Does a larger effective batch improve efficiency or quality?
runs.why: Checks throughput and optimization together; four times the batch means fewer updates.
runs.gate: Keep data passes fixed, report changed update count and tokens/update. Do not equate equal steps with equal training.

runs.name: Batch × rate interaction
runs.question: Was the larger batch limited by its learning rate?
runs.why: A targeted interaction test avoids declaring batch 64 bad after one LR.
runs.compare: S09; LR doubled, not blindly multiplied by four.
runs.gate: Run only if S09 is promising or ambiguous. The 2× multiplier is our hypothesis, not a universal scaling law.

runs.name: LoRA, lower rate
runs.question: Can smaller trainable matrices match full SFT at lower cost?
runs.why: Use a separately chosen LoRA LR and meaningful capacity, not a deliberately weak adapter.
runs.compare: S12 and tuned full-SFT winner; match data, batch, context and epochs.
runs.gate: Qwen LoRA is not supported by the current main SFT wrapper. Implement/test module coverage, gradients, save/reload and export first.

runs.name: LoRA, higher rate
runs.question: Was lower-rate LoRA under-trained?
runs.why: A fourfold adapter LR contrast; avoid borrowing full-model LR.
runs.compare: S11; only LoRA peak LR changes.
runs.gate: Same Qwen adapter implementation gates as S11; do not promise a memory or speed saving before measurement.

runs.name: Shorter-context cost test
runs.question: Can we retain task gains with less history per example?
runs.why: Long context may dominate compute; this tests that cost explicitly, not by silently throwing away long traces.
runs.gate: Optional study, not a default change. Rebuild examples with audited target coverage, original recorded compactions and explicit earlier-history loss. Recount examples and tokens.

runs.name: Repeat selected recipe · seed 43
runs.question: Does the selected recipe repeat with a new training seed?
runs.why: One fortunate run is weak evidence. Repeats are worth more than another cosmetic parameter change.
runs.compare: Selected completed SFT recipe, including its data, schedule and method.
runs.gate: Select any fully specified completed SFT row on Fleet dev; pin its actual recipe. Keep evaluation seeds fixed.

runs.name: Repeat selected recipe · seed 44
runs.question: How variable is the selected training result?
runs.why: Three total training seeds separate run variation from rollout noise.
runs.gate: Same frozen corpus and evaluation protocol; final Fleet and WEB do not select the recipe.

rl.title: RL · a smaller follow-on study
columns: Research priority. No RL jobs are launched by this page.
Exact base or a selected, accepted SFT checkpoint; pin its hash before launch.
Proposed policy update learning rate, constant in this initial RL comparison.
Distinct training task prompts sampled per collected update.
Fresh scored attempts per task; all attempts use the same task version.
Collected optimizer updates, not tool calls. One optimization pass per collection.
262,144 live tokens plus validated native compaction; long episodes remain allowed.
All rows wait for proven reward collection, a finite update and a reloadable checkpoint.

runs.name: Base RL anchor
runs.question: Does verified on-task reward improve held-out success?
runs.why: Begin with an interpretable full learning run after one real update/reload is proven.
runs.gate: Exact reward evidence, reward variation, saved/reloadable checkpoint and validated long-episode compaction are prerequisites—not claims of current readiness.

runs.name: Stronger RL rate
runs.question: Is the anchor update too small?
runs.why: A threefold range before exploring many algorithm settings.
runs.gate: Identical task sampling, seeds, update budget and reward code to R01.

runs.name: Start RL from accepted SFT
runs.question: Does SFT give RL a better starting policy?
runs.why: A valuable treatment after an SFT checkpoint is selected independently.
runs.gate: Pin accepted SFT checkpoint hash; not automatically eligible until chosen. Compare against R01, not a different harness.

runs.name: More attempts, same collection size
runs.question: Is deeper exploration per task better than wider task coverage?
runs.why: Both R01 and this row collect 32 attempts per update; episode runtime can still differ.
runs.gate: Report task coverage and actual valid attempts; technical failures are excluded, never assigned zero reward. Real uniform rewards remain valid but give no relative signal.
runs.compare: R01; task breadth versus attempts per task, not a pure group-size effect.
